explanation: An interface can display an edit or newly created item before its background save, multi-step creation or notification processing has finished. This pattern matches reports that interrupt that unfinished work with a hard refresh, immediately run the previously saved configuration or check results before processing completes, then call the old state loss of a completed operation. Verify the actual completion and reread the same item or recipient. Acknowledged-save loss, ordinary navigation discarding valid edits, or an effect still absent after completion needs separate evidence.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as an administrator and open Data permissions > Groups at /admin/permissions/data/group. Type Administrators into Search for a group and wait ten seconds. Inspect whether All Users remains visible, then press Ctrl+A without changing the query or clear and retype it. The rejected report expected: Searching for Administrators filters the group list to Administrators. It claimed this outcome: The report says Administrators and All Users remain visible after typing the query and waiting ten seconds; pressing Ctrl+A or clearing and retyping makes All Users disappear. Review concluded: The agent captured the screenshot before the group search was applied and mistook the unfiltered list for the completed search result. This is a premature observation, not evidence that searching for Administrators returns All Users.

explanation: A setup helper can require a particular input format even when another notation looks equivalent. Reviewed Metabase examples include SQLite connection strings requiring sqlite:///, with four slashes for an absolute Unix path; 64-character embedding secret keys accepting lowercase hexadecimal; and a lone opening quote being incomplete filter syntax rather than a literal quote. A Spark connection string outside the form's advertised syntax was also rejected while supported input worked. This pattern matches assuming those unsupported forms must work; a failure for the promised format or an accepted value being overwritten is different.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Unsaved form only; do not submit a connection attempt. Both tested paths are illustrative and need not exist for client-side prefill. In Admin > Databases, select Add database and choose SQLite. Enter jdbc:sqlite:/tmp/DBQA-fixture.sqlite in Connection string (optional) and blur the field. Observe Filename remains empty. Replace the URI with the reported two-slash form jdbc:sqlite://C:/path/to/database.db and blur. Observe Filename remains empty again. The rejected report expected: Entering an accepted SQLite connection string should prefill the fields below, including Filename, per the note 'You can use a connection string to pre-fill the details below'. It claimed this outcome: Both reported SQLite strings (one- and two-slash forms) are rejected with a red "Couldn't use this connection string." message, so Filename stays empty. The form's actual example (jdbc:sqlite:///C:/path/to/database.db, three slashes) fills Filename correctly (control). Review concluded: The SQLite parser intentionally requires sqlite:///; upstream unit and e2e tests cover only that form.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Databases > Add a database and select SQLite. Enter a unique display name and Filename /tmp/qa-does-not-exist/database.sqlite. Enter jdbc:sqlite:///tmp/qa-does-not-exist/third.sqlite in Connection string, then click Display name. Inspect the populated Filename. The rejected report expected: Prefilling the absolute SQLite path should preserve /tmp/qa-does-not-exist/third.sqlite rather than change it to a relative path. It claimed this outcome: Paste jdbc:sqlite:///tmp/x.sqlite (absolute Unix path). Filename becomes tmp/x.sqlite (leading slash dropped) and the form still says pre-filled. The Windows placeholder example and manual entry keep the path correctly (control). Review concluded: Works as intended: under the common sqlite:/// convention three slashes give a relative path, and an absolute Unix path needs four slashes (sqlite:////tmp/x), which Metabase prefills correctly.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin open Admin > Embedding with guest embeds enabled and a generated key. Replace Embedding secret key with AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (64 uppercase A characters). Blur the field. Observe validation error; refresh the page. The rejected report expected: A valid 256-bit hexadecimal key accepts uppercase A–F, or the form clearly states it requires lowercase and normalizes the equivalent hexadecimal encoding. It claimed this outcome: The 64-uppercase-A key is rejected with an 'Assert failed: Invalid embedding-secret-key! Secret key must be a hexadecimal-encoded 25...' error toast. Refresh restores the prior generated key, although A is a valid hexadecimal digit. Review concluded: Works as intended: the secret-key validation accepts lowercase hexadecimal only; lowercasing the key saves it.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As the supplied admin, open Admin > Databases > Add a database. Select Spark SQL in a fresh unsaved form. Enter jdbc:sparksql;Server=qa-spark.test;Port=10001;Schema=qa_schema in Connection string (optional). Click Display name and inspect Host and Port. The rejected report expected: Entering a valid Spark SQL connection string prefills the separate connection fields such as Host and Port. It claimed this outcome: Host and Port remain empty with their default placeholder values after entering the connection string. Review concluded: Works as intended: the reported jdbc:sparksql; string doesn't match the documented format, and the form says it couldn't use the string. A string in the documented format pre-fills Host.

explanation: A PostgreSQL database connection address can encode characters, for example representing a space as %20. In the reviewed prefill form, that encoded database name remained visible but the server decoded it correctly and the connection succeeded. This pattern matches calling the displayed representation corruption without checking its actual use; decoding it prematurely could also alter a name containing a literal percent sign. A valid connection name actually misinterpreted or made unusable is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin, open Databases > Add database and select PostgreSQL. Enter postgresql://dbqa%40user:p%40ss%3Aword@dbqa.invalid:5433/dbqa%20test?sslmode=verify-full in Connection string (optional) and blur. Read the Database name and Username inputs. The rejected report expected: URI prefill should decode dbqa%20test to the database name 'dbqa test', just as it decodes dbqa%40user to dbqa@user. It claimed this outcome: Paste a PostgreSQL URI with a percent-encoded database name (…/dbqa%20test). Database name and the auto display name keep the literal %20, while username, password and query params are decoded. Unencoded names fill correctly (control). Review concluded: The encoded database name is the working form: the server decodes it, so the connection succeeds. Only the displayed field text keeps %20, and decoding in the form could break names that contain a literal percent sign.

explanation: An administrator-authored field can deliberately accept flexible text, including relative addresses, templates or partial reusable code. This pattern matches a report that assumes the form must reject every value that looks incomplete or unusable, without establishing a restrictive format requirement for that field. Saving the user's own free-form content is not sufficient evidence that the application generated or corrupted an invalid value. Test valid supported input and distinguish an explicit validation promise from a preferred restriction.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, open Admin > Settings > Maps. Replace Map tile server URL with not-a-url and move focus away. Observe Changes saved and reload. The rejected report expected: A value that is not a complete URL is rejected with a validation message. It claimed this outcome: not-a-url or a scheme-only https:// saves with Changes saved and persists after reload; pin maps then show no basemap. Review concluded: Works as intended: the setting has no validation, and the docs allow a relative path as well as an http(s) URL, so not-a-url is a legal value and https:// saves the same way. A well-formed but unreachable URL breaks the map the same way.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as administrator and open /admin/settings/notifications. Click Add a webhook (or Add another). Enter https://example.test/qa-webhook as Webhook URL, QA Blank Auth as name, and QA description as Description. Select API Key authentication and keep Header selected. Leave both Key and Value blank. Click Create destination. Reload the settings page and reopen QA Blank Auth. API Key/Header remains selected with empty Key and Value. The rejected report expected: Selecting API Key authentication should require a nonempty key and value before creating or saving the destination. It claimed this outcome: Create destination succeeds with API Key and Header selected but empty Key and Value. Reloading and reopening the destination retains this incomplete configuration. Clearing previously populated Key/Value and saving is also accepted. No delivery failure is claimed. Review concluded: Works as intended: nothing documents or requires API-key webhook auth to have a non-empty key and value.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as an admin and open /admin/settings/notifications. Click Add a webhook. Enter URL https://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts, name 'QA FTP check 7731' and description 'ftp repro 7731'. Keep Authentication method set to None and click Create destination. Click the new webhook card to open 'Edit this webhook'. Change Webhook URL to ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts and click Save changes. The modal closes with no error. Refresh the page and click the webhook card again. Webhook URL shows ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts. The rejected report expected: Saving should be rejected and the form should show "Please enter a correctly formatted URL", because only http: and https: webhook URLs are allowed. It claimed this outcome: The modal closed after Save changes and no error appeared. After a refresh, reopening "Edit this webhook" showed the Webhook URL as ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts. Review concluded: Works as intended: the webhook URL field accepts any well-formed URL; an unusable scheme is the admin's input choice.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Temporary provider configuration is authorized only while preserving password login and all account credentials. Restore Google to unconfigured immediately via Authentication Overview > Google menu > Deactivate > confirm; this clears client/domain. As Admin open Authentication > Google auth with provider unconfigured. Enter syntactically accepted Client ID qa-maps-auth.apps.googleusercontent.com. Enter https://invalid-domain/path in Domain and click Save and enable. Observe Success then reload and inspect Domain. The rejected report expected: Reject a scheme/path URL as invalid for the email-domain field and retain the form for correction. It claimed this outcome: Save displays Success, then reload retains https://invalid-domain/path. Review concluded: Works as intended: the Google sign-in domain is a plain admin-entered value with no documented format; saving it as typed is not broken behavior.

explanation: A webhook can send a request to another service using a Basic authentication username and password. The reviewed report objected that this password was readable in its authorized configuration form, but no requirement for that particular field to hide the characters was established. This pattern matches a masking complaint on that basis alone, without an unauthorized viewer or a masking promise being violated. Verify who can see the field; actual disclosure outside the allowed audience is a different security claim.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, open Admin > Settings > Notifications and add a webhook. Select Basic authentication. Type a password and observe it is readable. The rejected report expected: The webhook Password field masks the entered secret. It claimed this outcome: Typing into the Basic authentication Password field shows the password as readable text. Review concluded: Works as intended: nothing requires the webhook password field to be masked.

explanation: A form can correctly refuse invalid input and preserve the saved value without using the reporter's preferred error phrase, extra message or additional red outline. This pattern matches those reviewed feedback preferences when valid corrections work and no applicable requirement for the requested treatment is established. Verify the actual rejection, recovery and saved state rather than judging only the wording. Proven silent refusal, misleading success, an applicable accessibility requirement or inability to recover is outside this narrow rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, open Admin > People > Groups and create a group. Choose Edit Name, enter three spaces, and click Done. Observe the generic error dialog. The rejected report expected: A whitespace-only group name is rejected with field validation, as an empty name is. It claimed this outcome: Done is enabled for three spaces; clicking it opens a generic Something went wrong dialog. The original name is kept. Review concluded: Works as intended for labeling purposes: the server rejects the blank name and the original name is kept; specific validation copy here is not a hard requirement.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Harbor Admin, create a uniquely named PeopleQA-Groups fixture. Open its ellipsis > Edit Name. Enter PeopleQA-Groups-Edge-5329 followed by ten repetitions of -ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ (295 characters total). Click Done. The rejected report expected: A user-friendly validation error message explains the group name length limit without exposing internal database errors. It claimed this outcome: A dialog displays raw SQL exception details: 'Value too long for column "NAME CHARACTER VARYING(255)": ... (295)"; SQL statement: UPDATE "PERMISSIONS_GROUP" SET "NAME" = ? WHERE "ID" = ? [22001-214]'. Review concluded: Works as intended: an overlong group name is rejected and the original name is kept, as with admin-030; specific validation wording is not required.

explanation: A test must actually activate the control whose behavior it claims to measure. This pattern matches reports where the input reached a neighboring element or popup, a drag never reached the required threshold, the editor was in the wrong mode, or a simulated key combination differed from the real shortcut. A click timeout or text appearing elsewhere therefore does not establish failure of the intended link, input or command. Confirm the event target, focus and complete gesture, then repeat the same intended action correctly before alleging its failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Authenticate as the Harbor account by loading the supplied saved authentication state. Navigate to /admin/datamodel/database. Expand Sample Database in the left sidebar and select Accounts. Select the ID field and verify the panel shows ID, BIGINT, and Entity Key. Select Email in the Accounts field list. Observe the Email card and the URL /admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/6/field/24. The right-side panel still shows ID, BIGINT, and Entity Key after waiting six seconds; repeat selecting ID and then Email to confirm the mismatch persists. The rejected report expected: After selecting Email in Accounts, the settings panel should show Email and that field’s metadata/settings, consistent with the page’s instruction to select a field to edit its settings. It claimed this outcome: The Email card became highlighted and the URL changed to /admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/6/field/24, but the right panel continued to show ID as the field name, BIGINT as its data type, and Entity Key as its semantic type. This remained visible after waiting six seconds and after repeating the ID-to-Email selection. Review concluded: Selecting Email's field card navigates to field/62 and shows EMAIL and CHARACTER VARYING, including after repeating ID then Email. Clicking its editable name instead does not select field details; field/24 is ID.

explanation: These reports were rejected by a reviewer as intended behavior, but the record does not explain why. This is a holding group, not an established reusable explanation of what the model misunderstood. A new report can be compared with the exact rejected action and outcome in the example, but similar wording alone is insufficient to declare it intended. Recover the missing rationale or obtain new evidence before applying a more specific rejection rule.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Release operations, Tables in Release operations, and Release Requests. Edit the table, set its display name to a distinct nonempty QA name and save; verify it persists. Edit again, clear the display name completely, and click Save. Observe the editor closes showing the prior name. Reload and reopen Edit. The rejected report expected: An invalid empty name should be rejected with clear validation, or an allowed clearing should be stored/reset explicitly; Save should not silently discard the input. It claimed this outcome: After submitting an empty name, the editor closed and retained QA Reference Release Requests. Reload and reopening Edit still showed the prior name. A full-page AI assertion confirmed no validation error or warning was shown. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, note the current Allowed domains for iframes in dashboards so you can restore it afterwards. Open Admin > Settings > General and scroll to Tables, X-Rays and domains. Replace Allowed domains for iframes in dashboards with not a domain and blur. Observe Changes saved; refresh General and inspect the saved domain list. The rejected report expected: A setting for allowed domains should reject hostnames containing spaces and explain the invalid entry instead of saving it as a usable domain. It claimed this outcome: The literal not a domain is accepted with Changes saved and remains after refresh. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Settings > Localization. Scroll to Numbers and open Separator style. Choose 100.000,00; observe selected format and Changes saved. Refresh and scroll back to Numbers. The rejected report expected: The saved 100.000,00 separator format should remain selected after refresh. It claimed this outcome: The dropdown initially changes to 100.000,00 and shows Changes saved, but after refresh it displays 100,000.00 again. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin, open Sample Database > Products > Price in Table Metadata. Open Preview; scroll field settings to Multiply by a number. Enter -1.25 and blur; refresh and reopen preview to verify saved negative values such as -36.83. Replace multiplier with abc and press Tab. Observe emptied multiplier and original positive preview values; refresh and reopen preview. The rejected report expected: Reject nonnumeric multiplier with validation feedback, retaining the previous saved multiplier rather than saving an empty reset. It claimed this outcome: Entering nonnumeric text leaves the multiplier input empty; on blur, the saved -1.25 multiplier is cleared with a 'Formatting of Price updated' toast, preview values revert from negative (-36.83) to positive (29.46), and the reset persists across a page reload without any validation error. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin open Databases > Add database; leave PostgreSQL selected to create a fresh unsaved form. Enter postgresql://qa_user:examplePass@database.example.com:6543/qa_database in Connection string; blur it and observe Port 6543. Replace the entire string with postgresql://qa_user:examplePass@second.example.com/second_database and blur. Inspect Host, Database name and Port. The rejected report expected: The replacement PostgreSQL URL without an explicit port uses default port 5432, rather than a stale port from a different URL. It claimed this outcome: Host updates to second.example.com and Database name to second_database, but Port remains 6543. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review.

explanation: A configured query or workflow can be invalid because its author selected incompatible data types, references, relations or duplicate field names. This pattern matches a report that treats the resulting clear, recoverable error, or a failed test of an invalid draft, as failure of a valid supported configuration. First repair the stated configuration problem and run a valid control; the ability to edit or test a draft does not by itself promise that every invalid combination is blocked earlier. Corruption of a valid definition or loss of unrelated saved data is outside this rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Use disposable SEG-QA segments on Sample Database / People. Observed second fixture was SEG-QA-Dependent-20261019 and referenced retired SEG-QA-People-20261019-v2 before adding itself. Its preview worked immediately before adding the self-reference. Create a disposable People segment filtered to State CA. Create a second disposable segment referencing the first; verify Preview returns 90 rows. In the observed setup the first segment was subsequently retired, and the second still previewed successfully. Edit the second segment, click Add filter and select that same second segment as an additional filter. Enter a change reason and click Save changes. Reopen the segment and click Preview. Open Show error details. The rejected report expected: The editor should prevent selecting or saving a circular self-reference, with actionable validation rather than saving an unusable definition. It claimed this outcome: The segment saves and retains its own name as a filter. Preview fails with 'There was a problem with your question' and 'Segment expansion failed. Check mutually recursive segment definitions.'. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review: saving is allowed and Preview explains the recursive definition.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Add database > Presto; enter host qa.invalid, port8080, catalog mo_catalog, schema mo_schema, username mo_qa and a display name. Enable Authenticate with Kerberos under advanced options. Enter Kerberos principal mo_qa@QA.INVALID and cache-file path /tmp/mo-qa-missing-cache. Save. The rejected report expected: The offered Kerberos principal input should be supported; unavailable credentials or host can produce an appropriate authentication/connection failure. It claimed this outcome: Save fails with 'Connection property KerberosPrincipal is not allowed' rather than accepting the form's own principal property. Review concluded: Works as intended: Presto requires the Kerberos coordinator service for Kerberos auth. The form does not mark required fields and the placeholder is an example, so the rejection of an incomplete config is driver validation with imprecise wording.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin create a fresh SegQA-prefixed segment A on Sample Database Products with Category is Gadget; enter name/description after choosing filter, save. Create segment B on Products filtered only by A; save and reopen B to verify 53 rows. Open A and add B as another filter; supply a revision reason and Save changes. Reopen B, whose definition has not changed, and click Preview; switch to the newly opened tab. The rejected report expected: Reject the edit that introduces a circular dependency, keeping the existing dependent segment B usable. It claimed this outcome: A saves successfully referencing B while B references A. Preview displays 'There was a problem with your question' and 0 rows. Neither segment directly references itself. Review concluded: Works as intended for labeling: consistent with data-modeling-146, saving a recursive segment definition is allowed and the query error names the recursive definition.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: In Admin > Table Metadata > Segments create a fresh uniquely named D segment on Sample Database > Accounts, with description and Active Subscription is true; save. Create a fresh E segment on the same table, with description and D as its only filter; save. Open E and verify its count (observed 464 rows), then return to the list. Edit D, add E as another filter, enter a change reason, and Save changes. The list now shows D referencing E and E referencing D. Open E again. The rejected report expected: Saving a circular dependency should be prevented with clear validation so both segments remain usable. It claimed this outcome: Saving D succeeds without rejecting the cycle. E still opens with its D filter, but its formerly displayed 464-row count is absent. A whole-page AI assertion confirmed no numeric row count is displayed. Review concluded: Works as intended: segments can reference each other, and a cycle breaks the dependent segment's count, as in admin-337.

explanation: A connection-string helper fills individual database settings from a supplied string, but it may update only fields that the new string actually specifies. This pattern matches a report that replaces the string, omits a setting such as Port, and assumes a previously visible valid port must be cleared automatically. Retaining that visible value is allowed under the reviewed prefill behavior. Supplying an explicit new port that is ignored, or a hidden old value overriding the displayed configuration, is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Databases > Add database and select MySQL. Enter jdbc:mysql://qa_user:qa_pass@db.example.test:3307/qa_db?ssl=true and blur. Confirm fields show host db.example.test and port 3307. Replace the URI with jdbc:mysql://qa_second:second_pass@second.example.test/second_db and blur. Inspect host, database, username and Port. The rejected report expected: When replacing the connection string with one that omits the port, the Port field should clear or revert to the default (3306) rather than retaining the previous custom port. It claimed this outcome: Host, database name, and username update to match the new connection string, but the Port field remains filled with 3307 from the previous connection string. Review concluded: Works as intended: connection-string prefill only fills fields the string provides; upstream e2e tests assert a portless string keeps the existing Port.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin, open Databases > Add database and choose PostgreSQL. Paste postgresql://qa:pass@localhost:5433/dbqa into Connection string and blur. Port shows 5433. Replace it with postgresql://qa:pass@localhost:notaport/dbqa and blur. Inspect Host, Username and Port. The rejected report expected: A non-numeric port is rejected with a validation message, or the stale port is cleared. It claimed this outcome: Host and Username update from the new string, Port keeps the previous value 5433, and no error is shown. Review concluded: Works as intended per human review: the same port-retention behavior as metabase-admin-b76.

explanation: The public address and network proxy settings of an installation affect generated links and redirects. A wrong public address can produce unreachable links, and a proxy that fails to tell the application the original request used HTTPS can cause a redirect loop. This pattern matches a report that attributes those demonstrated setup problems to application behavior under a correctly configured installation. Verify the external address and required forwarded scheme information; failures that remain with correct supported configuration require independent investigation.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as an administrator at / and open /admin/settings/general. Ensure Redirect to HTTPS starts Disabled. Enable Redirect to HTTPS and wait for Changes saved. Open /admin/settings/general in a fresh tab or reload the HTTPS page. Observe the browser's ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS error. Inspect the network: HTTPS requests receive 301 redirects to their identical HTTPS URLs. The rejected report expected: Already-HTTPS requests should load normally after enabling HTTPS redirects. Only HTTP requests should redirect to HTTPS. It claimed this outcome: Immediately after enabling the switch at 16:59:22 UTC, fresh HTTPS Admin navigations failed in multiple browser sessions with ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS. Network evidence shows repeated HTTP 301 responses whose Location is the exact same HTTPS request URL (for example /admin/settings/general?qa-recovery=1). A new query string also loops. The setting was restored with a narrow cleanup PUT false from a still-open page; cached permanent redirects also needed refreshing. Review concluded: Fixture issue: the sandbox proxy terminates TLS without forwarding the original scheme, so Metabase sees every request as HTTP and redirects. With a correct proxy header the same requests succeed.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: No database was created. URLs are disposable test values, not working credentials. Exact relevance of the encoded URL or advanced options to this failure is uncertain. Open Admin > Databases > Add database (PostgreSQL). Enter disposable connection string postgresql://qa_user:qa_demo@localhost:5432/qa_connection and blur. Replace it with postgresql://qa%40user:demo%40pass@localhost:5433/qa%20connection?sslmode=require and blur. Scroll down, expand Show advanced options, and verify JDBC options show sslmode=require. Click Cancel, then Discard changes in the confirmation dialog. The rejected report expected: Discard the new unsaved connection and return to the working database list. It claimed this outcome: Database list route displays 'Something’s gone wrong' with refresh/back advice. Show error details displays only 'An error occurred'. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so every API call returned 301; discarding the form returns to the database list normally.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin, exit Admin, use New > Dashboard to create and save an empty disposable dashboard in Our analytics (used only as prerequisite context). Use New > Question, choose Sample Database > Orders, then click Save in notebook editor. Enter a fresh question name. Change save location from Release overview to Our analytics using location picker > Browse > Our analytics > Select this collection. Click Save. The rejected report expected: The new question is saved in the selected collection. It claimed this outcome: Save dialog stays open and displays “An error occurred”; assertion saw submit button temporarily labeled “Failed”. Question creation could not complete. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so follow-up API calls returned 301s; the same flow works normally.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin open Table Metadata > Segments > New segment. Select Sample Database > People. Add Source Is Google, enter a unique name and description, and Save changes. Reopen the segment; open Source filter, search Face, select Facebook as well, and Update filter. Enter reason for changes and Save changes. Reopen segment and verify Google and Facebook selected with 1015 rows. Open Source filter > operator Is > Is not > Update filter. The editor shows 1485 rows. Enter reason QA exclude two sources and Save changes. Inspect destination Segments list. The rejected report expected: Saving the valid exclusion segment returns to a usable list showing the new definition. It claimed this outcome: After Save changes the app navigates to /admin/datamodel/segments but replaces the list with 'An error occurred'. A settled-page assertion confirms this error state. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so follow-up API calls returned 301s; the same flow works normally.

explanation: Two names that look the same on screen can contain different permitted characters, such as a meaningful trailing space. This pattern matches a duplicate-name report that assumes validation must remove that whitespace and treat the names as identical despite the reviewed naming rules allowing the distinction. Compare the actual stored names and the promised normalization behavior. A collision between truly identical keys or a violation of an explicit trimming rule remains a separate claim.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Edit the second name to MO-comms-duplicate and save: observe Channel with that name already exists. Change it to MO-comms-distinct and save successfully. Edit the second name to 'MO-comms-duplicate ' (one trailing space), save and refresh. The rejected report expected: Duplicate-name protection should treat visually identical names consistently, rejecting or normalizing whitespace padding. It claimed this outcome: Exact duplicate name was rejected, but adding one trailing space allowed saving. After refresh both rows display MO-comms-duplicate, despite pointing to different destinations. Review concluded: Works as intended: channel names may contain spaces, so a trailing space makes a distinct name.

explanation: This benchmark is a curated evaluation with rules about which kinds of findings count. A report matches this pattern when its only established issue falls outside those rules, such as an accessibility-tree-only label problem with no accepted visible or pointer-driven failure, an invalid state reachable only through an API, or an expressly excluded exotic input. The mistake is assuming that every technical imperfection is eligible for this evaluation. Scope exclusion does not establish that the underlying issue is imaginary, and a separately demonstrated in-scope functional failure must be assessed independently.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as an administrator and open /admin/settings/maps. Click Add a map. Enter any map name and set the GeoJSON URL to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasets/geo-countries/master/data/countries.geojson, then click Load. Open “Which property specifies the region's identifier?” using a screen reader or inspect the browser accessibility tree. Observe that name, ISO3166-1-Alpha-3, and ISO3166-1-Alpha-2 are all announced/exposed as “[object Object]”. The region display-name selector has the same issue. The rejected report expected: Each property option exposes its actual property name (for example name or ISO3166-1-Alpha-3) as its accessible name. It claimed this outcome: After loading a valid GeoJSON, the accessibility snapshot shows all three choices as option “[object Object]”. Rendered DOM confirms each role=option has aria-label="[object Object]", despite visible text containing distinct property names. Reproduced on both identifier and display-name dropdowns. Review concluded: Not a product bug for labeling: the defect exists only in the accessibility tree and nothing visible or functional is broken.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin, open Admin → Table Metadata → Release operations → Release Requests (/admin/datamodel/database/2/schema/2:public/table/9). Click Sorting, then select Custom order. Use Tab to focus the Created At sortable field button. It is the last field in the original database order; its accessible description instructs Space to pick up and arrow keys to move. Press Space, ArrowUp, then Space. Observe Created At remains after Amount and no keyboard reordering occurs. Repeat with another field if desired. The rejected report expected: Following the sortable control's instructions—Space to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop—should reorder the field and save the custom order. It claimed this outcome: With Created At focused, trusted Space, ArrowUp, Space key events reach the sortable button, but data-is-dragging remains false and the order stays ID, Region, Category, Approved, Amount, Created At. Its aria-describedby instruction explicitly says to use these keys. Repeated after focusing via Tab. Mouse drag attempts were inconclusive and are not claimed as a separate defect. Review concluded: Not a product bug for labeling: the missing keyboard reorder is an accessibility-only issue with no visible or pointer-driven defect.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Metabase administration. Inspect the navigation logo link in the accessibility tree or run a link-name audit. The rejected report expected: The admin navigation logo link exposes an accessible name identifying its destination. It claimed this outcome: The focusable /admin logo link has an empty accessible name; the retained audit flags link-name. Review concluded: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open /admin/people and click Invite someone. Fill First name Keyboard, Last name Tester, and Email qa-keyboard@example.test. Press Shift+Tab to return to Email, then Tab again; the selector is skipped again. The rejected report expected: Groups should be a keyboard-focusable control that opens with Enter or Space and allows group selection without a mouse. It claimed this outcome: Groups is absent from the tab order. Focus moves directly from Email to Cancel, leaving group assignment inaccessible to keyboard-only users. Review concluded: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai and open /admin/people/groups. Observe the inactive top navigation links (Settings, Databases, Table Metadata, Permissions, Performance, Tools) and selected Groups sidebar label. The rejected report expected: Normal-size navigation text should meet a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio. It claimed this outcome: Top navigation text is #c8c8eb on #6363c5 at 13.6px normal weight (3.13:1); selected Groups text is #468bc7 on #daebf9 at 14px normal weight (2.98:1). Review concluded: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Settings → Authentication → API keys with at least one API key (tested with QA keyboard test in QA Analysts). Use keyboard navigation to focus Create API key. Press Tab twice. Observe focus leaves the page content and wraps to the Metabase logo link (/admin), skipping the pencil and trash actions. Repeat from Create API key; the same actions are skipped. Clicking the icons with a pointer does open the respective dialogs. The rejected report expected: Each API-key edit and delete control is a keyboard-focusable button with an accessible action name and can be activated with Enter/Space. It claimed this outcome: The pencil and trash controls appear as clickable images, never receive Tab focus, and are skipped when focus wraps from Create API key to the page's first navigation link. Reproduced twice; screenshots issue-002-before-tab.png and issue-002-after-tab.png capture the focus transition. Review concluded: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open /admin/permissions/collections/root as an administrator (or select Collections > Our analytics). The rejected report expected: Each editable access selector should be exposed as a named button or combobox, reachable by Tab and operable with Enter/Space and arrow keys. It claimed this outcome: The access selectors are omitted from keyboard navigation and expose no button/combobox role. Changing collection permissions requires a pointing device. Review concluded: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

explanation: A public execution page can deliberately display a generic failure message rather than expose internal errors or keep an editable retry form. In the reviewed case, the author also supplied a read-only database query to an action intended to write changes. This pattern matches an assumption that the generic public error proves a valid action failed or that detailed internal information must be revealed. Verify a valid write action and the public page's error contract before making either claim.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As primary admin, enable Model actions temporarily on Release operations database. In action settings enable Make public and save; follow matching Shared action forms public link from Admin Public sharing. Enter 827 into Qa Marker and submit the form. The rejected report expected: Submitting the form should either succeed or show an actionable inline error message while keeping the form available to edit and retry. It claimed this outcome: The form is completely replaced by a generic 'An error occurred.' page with no way to edit inputs or retry. Review concluded: Works as intended: the action's SELECT returns rows to a write executor, and public action pages deliberately hide error details behind a generic error screen.

explanation: An input can visibly change unsupported characters, dates or numeric precision while the user is still editing. This pattern matches a report that remembers the intended text and blames Save for a different result, although the field or preview already displayed that effective value before submission and the save preserved it. Observe the value immediately before saving and compare it with storage. A valid displayed value secretly replaced only during submission is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin Tools as the primary administrator and select Logs. Open Customize log levels. Replace Reset to defaults after duration with 0; observe positive-number validation. Replace the duration by typing 0.5 with the Minutes unit selected. Observe that the field instead displays 5 and Save is enabled. The rejected report expected: Typing 0.5 should retain the fractional duration or clearly reject it; it should not silently become 5. It claimed this outcome: Entering 0.5 through the keyboard renders 5 in Reset to defaults after, removes the positive-number validation error and enables Save. The default MULTIMODAL assertion confirmed the field displays 5, not 0.5. Review concluded: Works as intended: the input visibly shows the value it will save before Save, matching the visible-normalization precedent.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: In Admin > Table Metadata > Segments create a uniquely named Accounts segment on Sample Database with a description and Active Subscription is false; save. Open the segment and add or edit a Created At filter. Choose Relative date range, Previous, days. Replace the Interval with 1.5 and blur the input. Click Update filter, enter a change reason, and Save changes. Reopen the saved segment and its Created At filter. The rejected report expected: The interval should preserve 1.5 if fractional days are supported, or reject fractional input with clear validation; it should not reinterpret 1.5 as 15. It claimed this outcome: The input displays 15 without an error. The saved list definition and reopened date filter both show previous 15 days. Review concluded: Works as intended: the relative date interval takes whole numbers, and the field shows the value it will use before saving (same as dashboards-138).

explanation: A report's specific factual claim is contradicted by a decisive observation or by a controlled repetition of the same setup. For example, the allegedly deleted value is still present, or the allegedly broken control performs the requested action when activated as described. Match this pattern only when that counterevidence addresses the same value, action and conditions; a vaguely similar successful workflow is insufficient. The finding rejects the checked allegation, not every related defect or every possible historical failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: In Admin > Table Metadata > Segments, create a uniquely named QA segment on Sample Database > Orders with Total less than or equal to -1, a description, and save. Reopen the segment. Edit its Total filter from Less than or equal to -1 to Equal to -45.47, then click Update filter. Observe the editor's row count, then open Preview and inspect its results. Return to the segment editor and compare its row count with Preview. The rejected report expected: The segment editor's matching-row count should agree with the results of Preview for the same definition. It claimed this outcome: With the chip 'Total is equal to -45.47', the editor consistently displays '1 rows'. Its Preview displays 'No results!' and 'Showing 0 rows'. A subsequent whole-page assertion confirmed that the editor still shows 1 rows, not 0. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: fresh runs show 0 rows in both the editor and Preview.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Fresh setup: open Sorting, choose Alphabetical order, Done, then reload. Observe alphabetical field list. Open Preview > Detail, then Sorting; choose Auto-order, then Database order. Observe Database order ID, User ID, Product ID, Subtotal, Tax, Total, Discount, Created At, Quantity. Choose Auto-order again and Done. Observe same original order before refresh. Refresh and inspect the settled field list. The rejected report expected: The field order shown after choosing Auto-order and Done should match the order shown after reopening or refreshing the same table. It claimed this outcome: Before refresh, the list and Detail preview showed ID, User ID, Product ID, Subtotal, Tax, Total, Discount, Created At, Quantity. After refresh, the list instead showed ID, Created At, Discount, Product ID, Quantity, Subtotal, Tax, Total, User ID. A whole-page AI check confirmed the changed order. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce: Auto order re-sorts the list immediately to the same order shown after refresh; the before/after mismatch was misread.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Performance > Model persistence as administrator and enable persistence. Choose Custom, enter 0 9 15 * ?, blur and reload to confirm saved monthly schedule. Open Refresh models every and choose 24 hours. Inspect the selected schedule and custom input after saving settles. The rejected report expected: Choosing 24 hours should display 24 hours as the selected schedule. It claimed this outcome: After choosing 24 hours, the cron input disappears but the dropdown still displays Custom…. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: the dropdown shows 24 hours after selecting it.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as admin and open /admin/databases/2 (Release operations, Postgres). Confirm GET /api/database/2 shows is_full_sync: true, details.let-user-control-scheduling false/absent, and a daily cache_field_values schedule. Click 'Edit connection details', then 'Show advanced options'. Turn on 'Choose when syncs and scans happen'. Look at 'Scanning for Filter Values': it shows 'Never, I'll do this manually if I need to'. Click 'Save changes' without changing that select. GET /api/database/2: is_full_sync is now false and schedules.cache_field_values is null, so the scheduled scan was silently turned off. The rejected report expected: When the scheduling controls appear, they show the database's current behavior: 'Regularly, on a schedule' (is_full_sync = true) with its daily schedule. Saving without touching the scan option leaves is_full_sync = true and the scan schedule unchanged. It claimed this outcome: The scan selector appears as 'Never, I'll do this manually if I need to' (value 'none'), even though GET /api/database/2 shows is_full_sync: true and a daily cache_field_values schedule. After Save changes, GET /api/database/2 returns is_full_sync: false, is_on_demand: false, schedules.cache_field_values: null. If the database already has let-user-control-scheduling = true, the same form shows 'Regularly, on a schedule' correctly, so the wrong default only appears when the toggle is first turned on. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: the scan setting did not change to Never through the UI.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: In Admin Segments, choose New segment and select Sample Database > Orders. Add Created At > Relative date range, set Previous 7 days and enable Include today. Add the filter and enter a unique name and description. Save changes and inspect the table column, then reopen the segment. The rejected report expected: Saving retains the selected Orders table and its date filter. It claimed this outcome: The saved list and reopened editor identify Products instead of Orders. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: the saved segment kept its Orders table.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as administrator and open Admin > Table Metadata. Expand seeded Release operations and open Release Requests. If hidden, click its eye to unhide it and verify Hide table control. Click Hide table for Release Requests. Wait about one second for the Hid Release Requests notification, then immediately click Undo. Observe Change undone feedback and the table's visibility icon/control. The rejected report expected: Clicking Undo restores the table to its previous visible state with a normal eye icon. It claimed this outcome: The 'Change undone' notification appears, but Release Requests remains hidden with its crossed-out eye icon. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: Undo restores the hidden table.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Sign in as an admin. Go to /admin/settings/public-sharing and make sure Enable Public Sharing is turned on. Under Shared dashboards, find a dashboard that has a public link (in this run: MO-MAPS-QA-Public). Click its Public Link URL (/public/dashboard/c3c1afa6-...). Observe: the page stays on Admin Public sharing and no public dashboard tab opens. The rejected report expected: Clicking the public URL opens that public dashboard. It claimed this outcome: The URL stays at /admin/settings/public-sharing and the page looks the same. No /public/dashboard/ tab exists (SWITCH_TAB found only the admin page). Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: the public dashboard link opens.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Table Metadata > Sample Database > Reviews > Rating. Choose Custom mapping under Display values; save mappings (tested 1 to Poor QA and 5 to Excellent QA). Edit mapping again, restore those mapped values to 1 and 5, and Save. Open Display values dropdown and choose Use original value. The rejected report expected: Display values switches to Use original value while the table and field editors stay usable. It claimed this outcome: Both main metadata panels display An error occurred immediately after choosing Use original value. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review: Use original value removes the mapping and the metadata panels stay usable.

explanation: The browser's ordinary numeric representation cannot preserve every digit of arbitrarily large integers. This pattern matches a report that enters a number beyond its safe exact-integer range and assumes any rounding violates the field's contract without evidence that such precision is supported. Compare the value during typing, submission and storage, and test normal in-range values. An explicit exact-precision promise or corruption within the supported range requires separate assessment.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Performance > Database caching and select Adaptive. Enter 9007199254740993 in Minimum query duration. Save changes and reload. Focus Minimum query duration and press End to inspect its suffix. The rejected report expected: Retain the exact entered integer or reject an unsupported value with validation; do not silently save a different number. It claimed this outcome: The entered suffix 740993 changes to 740992 after save/reload. Readback assertion finds full value 9007199254740992; focusing and End visibly shows 740992. No rejection was shown. Review concluded: Works as intended: the value exceeds the largest integer the browser can represent exactly, so it rounds; no realistic cache duration is affected.

explanation: Some numeric controls represent whole numbers, such as a row count, retention period, offset or raw smallest currency unit. This pattern matches a report that enters a fraction into such a control and treats its reviewed rounding or rejection as loss of supported precision without establishing that fractions are allowed. Check the unit and supported domain, then compare an ordinary integer control. An integer changing incorrectly, a field promising decimals, or a hidden value differing from the accepted display is a separate claim.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin, open Table Metadata → Sample Database → Reviews → Rating. Scroll to Number of decimal places (initially blank). Enter 1.5 and blur the input. Refresh, reopen the formatting controls and read Number of decimal places. The rejected report expected: Reject fractional decimal-place counts with understandable validation rather than silently saving a different integer. It claimed this outcome: Entering 1.5 changed the field to 2 and displayed Formatting of Rating updated. Refresh retained 2. A whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no validation warning or explanation of rounding. Review concluded: Works as intended: the decimal-places field takes whole numbers and rounds a fractional entry.

explanation: When the same saved item is open in two tabs, one tab can be editing an older copy of its settings. Under the reviewed last-write-wins contract, saving that older copy may replace another tab's changes rather than merge the two edits or display a conflict warning. This pattern matches a report that assumes merging or conflict detection is guaranteed, despite the submitted older copy explaining the overwrite. A promised conflict-protection feature failing, or data disappearing without a competing save, is outside this rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin, create a fresh disposable PEOPLE-QA user using a unique test email and create a fresh PEOPLE-QA group under Groups. Add that user to the group. In tab A, open People > user's ellipsis > Edit user. Change only Last name and leave the dialog open. In tab B, open the group's details and remove that user with the row X. Verify the group shows 0 members. Return to tab A and click Update without changing Groups. Refresh group details in tab B. The rejected report expected: A name-only edit should preserve the completed membership removal, or warn about conflicting stale data rather than silently restoring access. It claimed this outcome: Group showed 0 members after removal. Saving only Last name to Concurrent restored the group in the People row. Refreshed group details showed 1 member, PEOPLE-QA Rowan Concurrent. Review concluded: Works as intended: the edit dialog shows and submits the user's group memberships, so saving it from an older view reapplies the groups it displays.

explanation: A query that appears to read one table can also need related tables to replace stored identifiers with human-readable names. This pattern matches a report that assumes permission for the visible base table is sufficient, then calls a permission error wrong even though those additional name lookups require access too. Identify the related data the query actually reads and test with the appropriate grants. A query failing after all required access is present is a separate permission claim.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, put Maya Chen in the dedicated group MO-PERM-1021. Leave All Users with no Sample Database access. Give the group granular Sample Database access with Orders set to Query builder and all other tables set to No, then save. Sign in as Maya Chen (maya@example.test). Open /browse/databases/1 (Databases > Sample Database). Orders is the only table listed. Click Orders and wait for results. Observe 'Sorry, you don't have permission to run this query.' and 'Showing 0 rows'. The rejected report expected: With Orders-only Query builder access, Maya should be able to run the plain Orders table query and see rows. It claimed this outcome: The Orders question opens with Filter, Summarize, and Editor controls available, but the result area says 'Sorry, you don't have permission to run this query.' and the footer shows 'Showing 0 rows'. A plain single-table query against Orders (limit 1) returns error_type missing-required-permissions. Review concluded: Works as intended: Orders displays User ID and Product ID as People and Products names, so the query joins those tables and requires access to them; documented in Metabase's permissions guide.

explanation: A menu, panel or narrow text field may show only part of its contents until the user scrolls, moves within the field or copies the complete value. This pattern matches a report that calls an option or value missing or incorrect from that initial visible slice, while the reviewed normal interaction reveals it in full and the control works. Inspect the complete content before alleging loss. Essential information that remains inaccessible through the supported interaction is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Products is allocated to metadata. Only metadata labels were changed, no DB rows. Restore Title Display as Text, Wrap text off, empty Link text and URL afterward. Related tables remain read-only. In Admin Table Metadata, select Sample Database Products and Title. Set Display as Link. Set Link text to 'Mo Products temporary display label with many words to exercise multiline wrapping without changing any database rows. This label should wrap into additional lines when text wrapping is enabled in this preview.' and Link URL to the Admin datamodel URL. Blur each input. Open Table preview and enable Wrap text. Refresh, reopen Preview and inspect rendered link labels. The rejected report expected: Wrap text should keep the full link label readable by wrapping all words properly within each cell. It claimed this outcome: Each preview cell renders two lines with the beginning and end of the text, but the middle phrase ('without changing any database rows') is missing/clipped. The issue persists after reloading the page and reopening the preview. Review concluded: Works as intended: the wrapped text is fully present; the preview column is wider than its panel and the rest is reachable by scrolling.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin, open Table Metadata, Sample Database, Reviews. Click empty area of Created At field card to open its settings. Click Preview, then Filtering. Choose Fixed date range. Observe the two-calendar Between mode at 1920×1080 desktop viewport. The rejected report expected: Both calendars and their date cells/navigation controls fit within or are reachable in the preview panel. It claimed this outcome: The second calendar extends past the preview panel and is clipped. Review concluded: Works as intended: the preview column is deliberately sized, and its container scrolls when the date picker is wider. The hidden days and the next-month arrow stay reachable by scrolling, and the preview has no submit button.

explanation: The report describes a failure, but independent review did not recover the claimed failing state under the stated conditions. This group records that evidence limitation rather than an established explanation of why the behavior was correct or why the original event occurred. A future report must match the same trigger and outcome and still needs its own reliable reproduction; resemblance to a nearby accepted bug is insufficient. Nonreproduction does not prove the event impossible or intended.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin > Permissions > Collections. Select Our analytics and observe the permission matrix. Reload the browser page. The rejected report expected: The selected Our analytics collection continues to show its permission matrix on reload. It claimed this outcome: Our analytics remains highlighted in the sidebar, but the main panel displays 'Select a collection to see its permissions' and does not show the permission matrix. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Comparison setup if needed: create a map from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johan/world.geo.json/master/countries.geo.json selecting name for both properties. Edit it, replace URL with the USA URL, click Refresh and save. This path loaded successfully. Test fixtures created earlier were deleted. As administrator open Settings > Maps and click Add a map. Enter a fresh name such as Mo Maps QA Validation. Enter not-a-url and click Load; observe invalid-location validation. Replace URL with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johan/world.geo.json/master/countries/USA.geo.json and click Load. Observe preview and property selectors. The rejected report expected: The valid USA GeoJSON loads a preview and property choices, consistent with the same URL working in Edit map. It claimed this outcome: The preview shows “An error occurred”; both property selectors remain Select… and Add map is disabled. Earlier, the same URL successfully loaded and persisted the United States preview when editing a map initially created from countries.geo.json. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Guest embeds were initially disabled; New embed/Agree and enable enabled them. The selected chart was initially unpublished. Parameter preview was exercised before publishing and reset to Disabled. As the primary Admin, open Admin settings, then select Embedding in the top navigation. Click New embed. If prompted, click Agree and enable for guest embedding. Select Chart, click Next, and choose the seeded Release requests by region and category chart (Browse/search Release if needed). This existing chart provides the fixture; no fixture creation is required. Click Next to reach Behavior, Parameters and Appearance. Leave Region and Category Disabled. Click Publish above the preview and inspect the settled screen. The rejected report expected: Clicking Publish should publish the chosen question for embedding and replace the instruction to publish, or provide an actionable error. It claimed this outcome: After clicking Publish, the modal still states “You will need to publish this question before you can embed it in another application” and retains Publish. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As primary admin, ensure Release operations database Model actions is enabled. Create a fresh SQL question in Our analytics root on Release operations with SELECT 24 AS qa_sharing_value; save with unique name and turn it into a model. Open the model's Info > Actions > New action. Enter SELECT {{qa_value}} AS qa_value and save it with a unique name; don't run it. On the saved model's Actions list, click the play control labeled Run for the new action. The rejected report expected: Run opens the action's user-facing form so its parameter can be supplied and submitted, rather than editing its definition. It claimed this outcome: Run opens a dialog with editable SQL, Action parameters configuration and Update button. the only Run link is the one behind the modal in the underlying list. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: In Admin Notification channels, create a webhook named QA-MAPS-header with an example.test URL and description. Click Add another. Enter URL https://qa-maps.example.test/second, name QA-MAPS-second, description QA-MAPS second fixture, and leave authentication None. Click Create destination and inspect the Webhooks list. The rejected report expected: Both destinations appear in the list after creation. It claimed this outcome: The dialog closed but only QA-MAPS-header was listed. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, open Table Metadata > Segments. Create an Orders segment with Total between 100 and 200, a name and description, then save. Edit the segment, change its name and description, enter a reason, and save. Inspect the definition column in the Segments list. The rejected report expected: Definition text uses the same English language as the surrounding page, such as “Filtered by Total is between 100 and 200.”. It claimed this outcome: Definition reads “Filtré par Total est compris entre 100 et 200” beside English NAME, TABLE, DEFINITION, Filter by table and New segment labels. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin Settings > General as the supplied administrator. Turn on the initially Disabled Custom homepage switch. Observe Enabled, then refresh the page. The rejected report expected: The enabled setting persists, or the UI explains why it cannot be saved. It claimed this outcome: The switch shows Enabled before refresh and Disabled after refresh. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As the fixture administrator, open Admin > Tools. Select Model cache log in the Tools sidebar. Observe the settled Model cache log page. The rejected report expected: The Model cache log page displays cache log records, an empty state, or an informative feature message. It claimed this outcome: The page displays 'An error occurred'. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Harbor Admin, duplicate Release requests by region and category to a disposable question in your personal collection. Open Admin > Embedding, enable guest embeds if disabled, and choose New embed > Chart. Select the copied question and continue to configuration. Set Region to Editable, enter initial value us-west, then change Region to Locked. Observe the two us-west rows. Set Category to Editable and enter Documentation into the Category input in the preview, pressing Enter. The rejected report expected: Preview filters to the matching us-west Documentation row (amount 90). It claimed this outcome: Preview displays “An error occurred in your query” and “An error occurred while running the query.”. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As primary admin open Settings > Maps. Create a fresh map named Mo Maps QA Countries, using https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johan/world.geo.json/master/countries.geo.json; Load and select name for both identifier and display name, then Add map. Click Remove on this map's row. In Delete custom map, click Yes and inspect the settled list. The rejected report expected: The confirmed custom map is deleted and removed from the Custom maps list. It claimed this outcome: The deletion dialog closes and a 'Changes saved' notification appears, but the custom map remains listed under Custom maps. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Harbor Admin use Invite someone to create a unique QA user with first/last name and example.test email. Click Create then Done. In People open the fresh user's ellipsis menu. Choose Deactivate user. Observe the settled page. The rejected report expected: Clicking 'Deactivate user' opens a deactivation confirmation dialog or deactivates the user with clear feedback. It claimed this outcome: The menu closes, but no confirmation dialog or notification appears, and the user remains listed unchanged. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an Admin, open Table Metadata and choose Release operations > Release Requests > Amount. Use this seeded numeric field as a disposable test field; record original settings for restoration, or use an equivalent newly connected test table with a numeric amount field. Set semantic type to Currency and leave visibility Everywhere. Scroll to Number of decimal places. Enter 3, then open Preview to verify a value such as 120.000. Close Preview, scroll back to Number of decimal places, and replace 3 with -1. The rejected report expected: Reject an invalid negative decimal count with validation while keeping table and field settings usable. It claimed this outcome: Typing -1 causes both metadata panes to display An error occurred. The decimal input disappears, so it cannot be corrected in the current editor. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: Open Admin Table Metadata as the authenticated admin and expand Sample Database. Select Products and open the Price field using its name row. Rename Price to Price QA metadata, blur to save, refresh, and restore its display name to Price. Open Semantic type and select Currency; observe the Products table and field list. The rejected report expected: Changing one field's semantic type should leave the table name and other fields' display names unchanged. It claimed this outcome: The Currency selection succeeds, but the table heading becomes PRODUCTS and unrelated field labels become EAN, TITLE, CATEGORY, VENDOR, RATING and CREATED_AT; sidebar still says Products. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As the supplied admin, open Embedding and select New embed. If guest embedding is disabled, choose Agree and enable. Keep Dashboard selected and click Next. Select Dark appearance, then open the Date Range Disabled menu and choose Editable. The rejected report expected: The dashboard preview updates to show the editable Date Range filter while continuing to display the dashboard cards. It claimed this outcome: The dashboard preview clears and displays a red error icon in the center of the dark preview area. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin, create a fresh disposable person through Invite someone with first name QA People, last name Explorer and a unique example.test email; keep default membership. Create a fresh disposable group with name mo-people-Équipe-20261028 (use a unique suffix if needed). Open that group from the Groups list and confirm its empty member detail. Click Add members, search for the disposable person's name and select it. Click Add beside the selected person. The rejected report expected: The selected user is added to the group and the group detail view displays the updated member list and count. It claimed this outcome: The group detail view is replaced by an error screen displaying "An error occurred". Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As primary admin, create a fresh disposable parent collection in Our analytics, then create a child inside it. In Admin > Permissions > Collections, verify All Users has Curate on both collections. On only the parent collection, change All Users to No access and Save changes > Yes. Leave child All Users access as Curate. Start a separate verified Jordan member session (not in a custom group granting parent access). Open the parent: it correctly says “Sorry, you don’t have permission to see that.”. Click the child collection shown in Jordan’s sidebar. The rejected report expected: The child collection loads and displays its contents and curation controls. It claimed this outcome: The main content area displays “An error occurred” while the collection remains selected in the sidebar. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

In Metabase, follow this workflow: As Admin, open Performance > Model persistence. Enable persistence if disabled, and confirm Refresh models every shows 6 hours. Open the refresh interval menu and choose 24 hours. Inspect the settled refresh interval. The rejected report expected: The selected 24-hour interval should replace 6 hours and be saved, or an error should explain why it could not be applied. It claimed this outcome: The menu closes and the interval remains 6 hours. A whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no explanatory error appears. Review concluded: Cannot reproduce on human review.

explanation: Typing into an editor does not establish that the new value was saved. This pattern matches reports that assume Enter, a scripted loss-of-focus event or an open editing form completed the operation, although the supported commit gesture never ran. Refreshing then correctly returns the previously saved value. Verify the applicable Save, outside click, Tab or other accepted action and its completion before reporting loss of a completed edit.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As an admin, open Admin > Table Metadata > Sample Database > Reviews. Rename the table to QA-TABLE Reviews and click outside the input; reload to verify this baseline persists. Change the table name to QA-TABLE Reviews café & <sample> and press Enter. Observe that the header and sidebar keep the old name, then reload: the name reverts to QA-TABLE Reviews. The rejected report expected: Pressing Enter to submit a new table name should save and persist the change after reload. It claimed this outcome: Pressing Enter does not update the sidebar or save the table name; upon page reload, the name reverts to the previous name ('QA-TABLE Reviews'). Review concluded: Works as intended: the table-name input saves on blur, not on Enter, and the documented save action (clicking away) persists the name. Pressing Enter just leaves an unsaved draft in the focused input.

explanation: A current interactive choice is not always a saved preference. In the reviewed cases, a filter reached through contextual navigation required an explicit saved view to survive refresh, and an embedding preview reloaded its configured initial values after a configuration change. This pattern matches an assumption that those temporary choices must survive automatically. Establish whether the value was actually saved; losing a completed saved setting or opening the wrong initial context is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: As admin open Embedding settings and enable guest embeds if disabled. Set Date Range to Locked and Date Grouping to Editable. In dashboard preview choose Date Grouping > Year. Observe year labels 2025 and 2026. In Previewing locked parameters choose Date Range > Previous 12 months. Observe Date Grouping loses Year and chart displays Q4 2025 through Q3 2026. The rejected report expected: Applying a locked Date Range preview value preserves the independently selected Year grouping on the dashboard. It claimed this outcome: Date Grouping loses the selected Year value and resets to default, causing the chart to revert from yearly to quarterly labels. Review concluded: Works as intended: changing a locked parameter regenerates the signed preview token, which reloads the preview from its configured initial values. Setting the grouping as an initial parameter value keeps it, so nothing is broken.

explanation: An input can deliberately handle blank or invalid text by clearing it, restoring the last valid value or applying a supported minimum instead of leaving an error. Reviewed Metabase examples include a relative date interval of zero becoming one day, invalid numeric text meaning no filter, and an empty required title or invalid typed date retaining the previous valid value. This pattern matches a demand for a different rejection style without evidence that a valid accepted value was lost. Check the field-specific rule and effective display; a valid value secretly replaced during submission is a different failure.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, follow this workflow: Create a disposable People segment with State is CA, unique name and description; save. Edit it and add Birth Date > Relative date range. Leave Previous selected, replace interval 30 with 0, keep day and Include today off. Click Add filter, enter revision reason, Save changes and refresh. Reopen the segment and click the Birth Date filter chip. The rejected report expected: Reject an unsupported zero-day interval with validation, or preserve the explicitly entered interval instead of silently changing it. It claimed this outcome: Zero is accepted without validation. The saved list says Birth Date is yesterday; reopening the picker shows Previous 1 day, silently changing the input from 0 to 1. Review concluded: Works as intended: a relative date interval must be at least 1, so 0 days is saved as 1 day (same as querying-367).
